sats.credit: Photo: Syced, via Wikimedia Commons (CC0). A 1/50 scale model of ALOS-4 at JAXA's Tsukuba Space Center.

k3.t: What is it? A radar satellite with the PALSAR-3 L-band synthetic aperture radar and a ship-tracking receiver.
Why does it matter? Forests cover 30% of the world's land, and deforestation is strongly linked to rising greenhouse gases .

what.t: A radar satellite with the PALSAR-3 L-band synthetic aperture radar and a ship-tracking receiver.

why.t: Forests cover 30% of the world's land, and deforestation is strongly linked to rising greenhouse gases.

impact.t: Tropical forests are often under cloud, which hides clearing from ordinary cameras. JAXA's ALOS-4 "DAICHI-4", launched July 1, 2024, carries the L-band PALSAR-3 radar, which sees through clouds and widens the observation swath from 50 km to 200 km at high resolution.

sats.alt: The GEDI forest-mapping laser mounted outside the Kibo module on the International Space Station

k3.t: GEDI is a laser tool on the International Space Station.
It shines light down on forests and times how long it takes to bounce back.
That tells scientists how tall trees are and how much carbon forests hold.

what.t: A lidar with 3 lasers that make 8 parallel tracks of measurements. Each laser spot is 25 meters wide, and GEDI measures canopy height, canopy structure and ground elevation.

what.name: University of Maryland, GEDI mission overview

why.t: Forests are changing fast. GEDI's 3D measurements help track forest carbon, biomass and habitat.

why.name: University of Maryland, GEDI mission overview

impact.t: GEDI has produced more than 10 billion high-quality observations of forest structure (University of Maryland).

impact.name: University of Maryland, GEDI mission overview

impact.t: For Further Information: University of Maryland, GEDI mission overview
Each GEDI laser spot on the ground is 25 meters wide, and spots are 60 meters apart.

k3.t: What is it? Twin satellites measuring Earth's changing gravity field.
Why does it matter? To track water in aquifers, ice and oceans, for drought and water planning.

what.t: Twin satellites measuring Earth's changing gravity field.

why.t: To track water in aquifers, ice and oceans, for drought and water planning.

impact.t: GRACE-FO, the US-German successor to GRACE (2002-2017), launched on May 22, 2018 and tracks Earth's water movement by measuring tiny changes in gravity. Its data reveal groundwater loss, ice sheet change and sea level rise; scientists using these satellites found Earth's total freshwater dropped abruptly starting in May 2014.

sats.n: Copernicus CO2M Carbon Dioxide Monitoring (ESA / EU)

k3.t: Some gases, like carbon dioxide , trap heat and warm our planet.
CO2M will be three satellites that measure how much of these gases people release.
That helps countries see if their plans to cut pollution are working.

what.t: Each satellite carries a near-infrared and shortwave-infrared spectrometer that measures carbon dioxide and methane in the air, focusing on emissions from human activity. It also measures nitrogen dioxide and tiny airborne particles.

why.t: Countries need an independent way to see whether their climate policies are cutting emissions and meeting Paris Agreement targets. CO2M will estimate emissions at local, national and regional scales.

impact.t: ESA and the European Commission expanded CO2M from two satellites to three, cutting the time to measure carbon dioxide around the whole globe to about 3.5 days.

impact.name: ESA, Europe’s carbon dioxide monitoring mission elevated to the power of three

impact.t: For Further Information: ESA, Copernicus Sentinel Expansion missions
Three CO2M satellites will measure human-made carbon dioxide around the whole globe in about 3.5 days.

k3.t: What is it? An ocean satellite with color, temperature and wind sensors.
Why does it matter? Continuity of ocean color and wind data for fisheries, cyclones and coasts.

what.t: An ocean satellite with color, temperature and wind sensors.

why.t: Continuity of ocean color and wind data for fisheries, cyclones and coasts.

impact.t: ISRO's EOS-06 is the third-generation satellite in the Oceansat series, launched on PSLV-C54 in November 2022. Its Ocean Color Monitor, Sea Surface Temperature Monitor and Ku-band scatterometer keep ocean color and wind data flowing for operational use; early images captured Cyclone Mandous and an algal bloom .

k3.t: What is it? A satellite with four instruments, including JAXA's Doppler Cloud Profiling Radar .
Why does it matter? Knowing whether clouds warm or cool the planet sharpens climate forecasts.

what.t: A satellite with four instruments, including JAXA's Doppler Cloud Profiling Radar.

why.t: Knowing whether clouds warm or cool the planet sharpens climate forecasts.

impact.t: Clouds and aerosols are among the hardest parts of the climate to measure. EarthCARE launched on May 29, 2024 with four instruments that measure them together.

k3.t: Earth gives off heat into space as invisible infrared light.
Part of that light, called far-infrared, has never been measured from space.
FORUM will measure it, helping scientists understand how Earth keeps its heat balance.

what.t: A satellite carrying a Fourier transform spectrometer to measure Earth's outgoing radiation in the far-infrared.

why.t: FORUM data will give unique insight into Earth's radiation budget and how it is controlled.

impact.t: FORUM will measure a part of Earth's outgoing radiation that has never been measured from space before (ESA).
For Further Information: ESA, FORUM
ESA calls the far-infrared a missing piece of the climate jigsaw that FORUM will fill in (ESA).

k3.t: Wildfires are much easier to stop while they are still small.
FireSat satellites carry special cameras that can sense heat from space.
They can spot a fire about the size of two parking spaces and help firefighters act fast.

what.t: FireSat is the first satellite constellation designed specifically for wildfires. Its infrared instruments can detect fires as small as 5 by 5 meters, about the size of two parking spaces, and measure how intense a fire is.

what.name: Earth Fire Alliance, FireSat first light (Sep 16, 2026)

why.t: The satellites we rely on today were not built for wildfires and miss detail and timing. FireSat data should reach fire agencies at least twice a day by the end of 2026, with global access expected by 2028 and an hourly global revisit by 2029.

why.name: Earth Fire Alliance, FireSat first light (Sep 16, 2026)

impact.t: The first three FireSats watched the front of the Big Grass Fire five times over three nights and two days, showing how it moved and faded (Earth Fire Alliance).

impact.name: Earth Fire Alliance, FireSat first light (Sep 16, 2026)

impact.t: For Further Information: Earth Fire Alliance, FireSat first light (Sep 16, 2026)
FireSat can detect a fire as small as 5 by 5 meters, about the footprint of two parking spaces.

k3.t: GCOM-C, also called SHIKISAI, is a Japanese satellite that looks at the whole Earth.
It sees clouds, tiny particles in the air, plants, ocean color, snow and ice.
This helps scientists understand climate change.

what.t: A satellite carrying SGLI, an optical sensor that sees from near-ultraviolet to thermal infrared light at 250 m to 1 km detail.

why.t: Long-term views of aerosols , clouds, plants and temperatures help explain climate change and improve climate models.

impact.t: SGLI collects global data once every 2 or 3 days on clouds, aerosols, ocean color, vegetation, snow and ice (JAXA).
For Further Information: JAXA, GCOM-C "SHIKISAI"
SGLI observes light from near-ultraviolet to thermal infrared, from 380 nanometres to 12 micrometres (JAXA).

k3.t: What is it? A satellite carrying TANSO-3 for greenhouse gases and AMSR3 for the water cycle.
Why does it matter? Countries need independent, consistent measurements of emissions to check climate pledges.

what.t: A satellite carrying TANSO-3 for greenhouse gases and AMSR3 for the water cycle.

why.t: Countries need independent, consistent measurements of emissions to check climate pledges.

impact.t: JAXA's IBUKI GW launched on June 29, 2025 on H-IIA No. 50.

k3.t: GeoXO will be new weather satellites that stay over the same spot above Earth.
They will watch storms, wildfires, smoke and floods as they happen.
This helps forecasters warn people sooner.

what.t: Satellites carrying visible and infrared imagers and a new hyperspectral infrared sounder for better forecasts.

why.t: In March 2026 the Commerce Department's Inspector General found GeoXO had made adequate progress, and noted a possible gap in data if older GOES satellites end before GeoXO is operating.

why.name: U.S. Department of Commerce OIG, Evaluation of NOAA's Progress Implementing the GeoXO Satellite Program (OIG-26-009-I)

impact.t: GeoXO will detect and monitor wildfires, smoke, dust, volcanic ash, drought and flooding, improving lead times for public alerts (NOAA).
For Further Information: NOAA NESDIS, GeoXO
The Inspector General made six recommendations to reduce the risk of a gap in geostationary weather data and improve risk management (OIG).

k3.t: INSAT-3DS is an Indian weather satellite that stays over the same place above Earth.
It takes pictures of clouds, rain, fog and fires.
It also passes on distress calls so rescuers can find people in trouble.

what.t: A weather satellite with a 6-channel Imager and a 19-channel Sounder, plus data relay and satellite-aided search and rescue.

why.t: It is designed for weather forecasting and disaster warning by monitoring land and ocean surfaces.

impact.t: INSAT-3DS payloads generate more than 40 geophysical data products, including rainfall, sea-surface temperature, fog, fire and smoke (ISRO).
For Further Information: ISRO, INSAT-3DS imaging Earth
INSAT-3DS had a lift-off mass of 2,275 kg and is built on ISRO's I-2k bus (Ministry of Earth Sciences).

k3.t: JPSS satellites fly over the North and South Poles, around and around.
They scan the whole Earth twice a day for temperature, clouds and rain.
Forecasters use the data to warn people before hurricanes and blizzards.

what.t: Satellites that measure atmospheric temperature and moisture, wind shear, land and sea surface temperature, clouds and rainfall rates.

what.name: NOAA NESDIS, NOAA satellites have you covered this hurricane season

why.t: They provide the majority of data that informs numerical weather forecasting in the U.S.

why.name: NOAA NESDIS, Joint Polar Satellite System

impact.t: Data from JPSS and other polar-orbiting satellites provide about 85% of the data used by weather prediction models (NOAA).

impact.name: NOAA NESDIS, NOAA satellites have you covered this hurricane season

impact.t: For Further Information: NOAA NESDIS, Joint Polar Satellite System
JPSS satellites orbit pole to pole 14 times a day, covering the whole globe twice daily (NOAA).

k3.t: What is it? The latest Landsat satellite, collecting 740 scenes of Earth each day, almost double its minimum requirement.
Why does it matter? The longest continuous satellite record of Earth’s land surface shows how forests, water and farms change.

How does it help people? Landsat supports water management in drought-prone regions where farms, industry and communities compete for water, and its free data added an estimated $25.6 billion to the U.S. economy in 2023.

what.t: The latest Landsat satellite, collecting 740 scenes of Earth each day, almost double its minimum requirement.

why.t: The longest continuous satellite record of Earth’s land surface shows how forests, water and farms change.

impact.t: Near-weekly Landsat observations enable tropical deforestation alerts, water quality monitoring and crop condition reports. NASA says Landsat’s free, public data contributed an estimated $25.6 billion to the U.S. economy in 2023 alone.
For Further Information: NASA, Landsat 9

k3.t: Sunlight brings energy to Earth, and Earth sends some back to space.
Libera will measure how much energy leaves our planet each day.
If more comes in than goes out, Earth warms, so this helps track climate.

what.t: An instrument that measures sunlight reflected by Earth and the infrared heat Earth gives off, from the top of the atmosphere.

why.t: The difference between the energy Earth absorbs and the energy it gives off is a key factor in our climate. More in than out means warming.

impact.t: Libera will continue the global record of Earth's energy budget kept by the CERES instruments since 2000 (NOAA).
For Further Information: NASA, Libera completes testing (Jan 30, 2026)
Libera is named for the daughter of Ceres in Roman mythology, a nod to the CERES instruments before it.

k3.t: What is it? The first MetOp Second Generation weather satellite, carrying the Copernicus Sentinel-5 air-quality instrument.
Why does it matter? To track air pollution, ozone and climate gases, and to sharpen weather forecasts.

How does it help people? Daily air-pollution data help authorities monitor pollution and make decisions, and better weather data matter: EUMETSAT notes extreme weather has cost Europe tens of thousands of lives over the past 40 years.

what.t: The first MetOp Second Generation weather satellite, carrying the Copernicus Sentinel-5 air-quality instrument.

what.name: ESA, First MetOp-SG satellite and Sentinel-5A launched

why.t: To track air pollution, ozone and climate gases, and to sharpen weather forecasts.

why.name: ESA, First MetOp-SG satellite and Sentinel-5A launched

impact.t: Sentinel-5 provides daily global data on air pollutants and trace gases such as ozone, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide, formaldehyde, carbon monoxide and methane , as well as aerosols and UV radiation. The data feed the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring and Climate Change services.

impact.name: ESA, First MetOp-SG satellite and Sentinel-5A launched

k3.t: Meteosat Third Generation is a team of weather satellites that watch Europe and Africa.
One camera takes a new picture of the weather every 2.5 minutes.
Another camera spots lightning, which helps warn people about dangerous storms.

what.t: Imager and Sounder satellites. The Imagers carry a Flexible Combined Imager and a Lightning Imager that sees lightning by day and night.

what.name: ESA, MTG-I2 completes Europe's latest weather trio

why.t: Lightning is a clear sign of turbulence linked to extreme weather, so spotting it early allows early warnings and storm tracking.

impact.t: MTG-I2 will deliver new images over Europe every 2.5 minutes, supporting early warnings and the tracking of wildfires and air pollution (ESA).

impact.name: ESA, MTG-I2 completes Europe's latest weather trio

impact.t: For Further Information: ESA, MTG-I2 completes Europe's latest weather trio
Around the world there are over three million lightning flashes every day (ESA).

k3.t: What is it? A radar satellite carrying NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band radars.
Why does it matter? Detecting ground and ice motion of about a centimeter helps with earthquakes, landslides, sinking ground, glaciers and crops.

what.t: A radar satellite carrying NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band radars.

why.t: Detecting ground and ice motion of about a centimeter helps with earthquakes, landslides, sinking ground, glaciers and crops.

impact.t: NISAR launched from India on July 30, 2025. Its two radars (NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band) see through clouds and darkness, scanning nearly all of Earth's land and ice surfaces twice every 12 days.

k3.t: OCO-2 is a satellite that measures carbon dioxide in the air.
It shows where the gas comes from and where plants and oceans soak it up.
It can even see plants glow faintly, which shows how healthy they are.

what.t: A satellite that measures carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, collecting around 100,000 measurements every day.

why.t: To find out precisely where carbon comes from and where it is stored, so scientists better understand how carbon is changing the climate.

impact.t: OCO-2 and its sister instrument OCO-3 on the space station show where carbon is emitted and where forests and oceans absorb it. Their data stay publicly available (Caltech).

impact.name: Caltech, NASA selects Caltech to operate the OCO missions (Aug 24, 2026)

impact.t: For Further Information: NASA, NASA and Caltech partner on two Earth science missions (Aug 24, 2026)

k3.t: What is it? A satellite whose hyperspectral Ocean Color Instrument measures light from ultraviolet to near-infrared.
Why does it matter? Phytoplankton feed ocean life and help move carbon; tracking them shows how the ocean and climate are changing.

what.t: A satellite whose hyperspectral Ocean Color Instrument measures light from ultraviolet to near-infrared.

why.t: Phytoplankton feed ocean life and help move carbon; tracking them shows how the ocean and climate are changing.

impact.t: PACE (Plankton, Aerosol , Cloud, ocean Ecosystem ) launched on February 8, 2024. Its hyperspectral Ocean Color Instrument tracks phytoplankton, tiny organisms that start the marine food web and drive the ocean's carbon cycle, and it shows how aerosols may feed their growth.
For Further Information: NASA, PACE mission

sats.alt: NASA/METI/AIST/Japan Space Systems and U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team (PIA23534)

k3.t: SMAP is a satellite that measures how wet or dry the ground is.
It can also tell if the soil is frozen or thawed.
This helps farmers and scientists get ready for floods and droughts.

what.t: A satellite with a radar , a radiometer and the largest rotating mesh antenna ever deployed in space, 20 feet (6 meters) wide.

why.t: Soil moisture links Earth's water, energy and carbon cycles, so mapping it improves predictions of weather, climate, floods and droughts.

impact.t: SMAP maps soil moisture and whether soils are frozen or thawed across the globe (NASA).
For Further Information: NASA, SMAP
SMAP's 20-foot (6-meter) "golden lasso" antenna is the largest rotating mesh antenna ever deployed in space (NASA JPL).

k3.t: What is it? A radar interferometer satellite that measures the height of water on land and at sea.
Why does it matter? Fresh water is unevenly measured on the ground; SWOT gives every country the same view of its rivers and lakes.

what.t: A radar interferometer satellite that measures the height of water on land and at sea.

why.t: Fresh water is unevenly measured on the ground; SWOT gives every country the same view of its rivers and lakes.

impact.t: SWOT (Surface Water and Ocean Topography) is the first global survey of Earth's fresh water. It measures more than 95% of lakes larger than 15 acres and rivers wider than 330 feet, tracking how much water flows through rivers and is stored in lakes and reservoirs.

k3.t: What is it? A satellite with a multispectral imager covering 13 spectral bands, with a 290 km swath and detail down to 10 m.
Why does it matter? To monitor agriculture, forests, land-use change, coastal and inland waters, and disasters.
How does it help people? Farmers use Sentinel-2 data to monitor crop health, predict yields and practice precision farming, and responders use it to map floods, wildfires and eruptions.

what.t: A satellite with a multispectral imager covering 13 spectral bands, with a 290 km swath and detail down to 10 m.

why.t: To monitor agriculture, forests, land-use change, coastal and inland waters, and disasters.

impact.t: Sentinel-2 revisits the same spot every five days at the equator with its two-satellite constellation. Its data support crop health monitoring and yield prediction, water quality monitoring, and disaster management for wildfires, volcanic eruptions and floods.

impact.name: ESA, Sentinel-2C joins the Copernicus family in orbit

impact.t: For Further Information: ESA, Sentinel-2 facts and figures

k3.t: Sentinel-3 satellites check the oceans, land and ice all the time.
They measure how warm the sea is, how high it is, and even spot fires.
Weather and ocean forecasters use this to keep people safe.

what.t: Satellites with instruments for ocean and land color (21 bands), sea and land temperature with two dedicated fire channels, sea height and more.

why.t: To monitor large-scale changes on Earth and provide near-real-time information for ocean and weather forecasting.

impact.t: Sentinel-3 data track sea-level change, sea temperature, water quality, sea ice, glacier melt, river and lake height, and wildfires (ESA).
For Further Information: ESA, Sentinel-3 facts and figures
Sentinel-3's temperature radiometer has two channels built just for spotting fires.

k3.t: Sentinel-4 is a space tool that watches the air over Europe.
It stays above the same spot and checks the air every hour.
This helps warn people when the air is dirty.

what.t: An ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared spectrometer that measures pollutants such as nitrogen dioxide and ozone .

why.t: Air pollution changes through the day, and hourly data can improve air quality forecasts.

impact.t: Sentinel-4's first images showed pollution hotspots such as Italy's Po Valley. It joins NASA's TEMPO and Korea's GEMS in watching air quality hourly from geostationary orbit .

impact.name: ESA, Sentinel-4 offers first glimpses of air pollutants

impact.t: For Further Information: ESA, Sentinel-4

k3.t: Sentinel-5P is a satellite that sniffs the air from space.
Every day it checks the whole planet for gases that make air dirty.
This helps keep people healthy and track gases that warm Earth.

what.t: The first Copernicus mission dedicated to monitoring our atmosphere. Its Tropomi instrument maps trace gases, aerosols and clouds.

why.t: The gases it maps affect the air we breathe, our health and our climate.

impact.t: Sentinel-5P provides daily global coverage of trace gases that affect air quality and climate (ESA).
For Further Information: ESA, Sentinel-5P facts and figures
Sentinel-5P's Tropomi instrument sees a strip of Earth 2,600 kilometers wide in one pass.

k3.t: What is it? A radar altimetry satellite that measures the height of the sea surface.
Why does it matter? An unbroken sea-level record helps coastal cities plan for rising water.

what.t: A radar altimetry satellite that measures the height of the sea surface.

why.t: An unbroken sea-level record helps coastal cities plan for rising water.

impact.t: Sea level rise is one of the clearest measures of a warming planet. Sentinel-6B launched on November 17, 2025 to continue the reference record of global sea level from space that began in the early 1990s, measuring sea-surface height with a Poseidon-4 radar altimeter and a microwave radiometer.

k3.t: TEMPO is a space tool that checks how dirty the air is.
It stays above the same spot on Earth and looks at North America every hour while the sun is up.
This helps warn people on bad air days so they can stay safe.

what.t: TEMPO, a spectrometer that measures air pollutants such as ozone and nitrogen dioxide.

why.t: Air pollution changes hour by hour, but older satellites passed over only about once a day.

impact.t: TEMPO is the first space instrument to measure North American air quality every daylight hour, at a resolution of a few square miles instead of about 100 square miles.
For Further Information: NASA, TEMPO instrument launches
NASA's TEMPO checks North America's air pollution every daylight hour from 22,000 miles up.

k3.t: What is it? A satellite that pinpoints methane and carbon dioxide plumes from individual sources.
Why does it matter? Finding single leaks lets operators and regulators fix them fast.

what.t: A satellite that pinpoints methane and carbon dioxide plumes from individual sources.

what.name: NASA, First greenhouse gas plumes detected

why.t: Finding single leaks lets operators and regulators fix them fast.

why.name: NASA, First greenhouse gas plumes detected

impact.t: Tanager-1 was built by Planet with a NASA JPL-designed imaging spectrometer for the nonprofit Carbon Mapper coalition. Its first published methane detection, on September 19, 2024, was a landfill plume in Karachi, Pakistan, with a preliminary estimated rate of 1,200 kg of methane per hour (Carbon Mapper estimate, reported by NASA).

impact.name: NASA, First greenhouse gas plumes detected
Carbon Mapper, first Tanager-1 detections (company release)
